model: HC feed-cost pass-through v1.0 (AMPC/Marsh method, re-estimated)
prose: Feed-cost pass-through check (AMPC/Marsh method, re-estimated on 2000-present USDA monthly data): each +10% in corn shaves about 2% off calf value with fed-cattle prices held constant, while a +10% fed-cattle move lifts calves about 14%. Right now, corn near $4.28/bu (-4% YoY) and fed cattle +11% imply calves about +17% vs a year ago; calves are actually running +24%, leaving roughly +8 points as herd-cycle scarcity beyond what feed and fed-cattle prices explain. Method borrowed from MSU AMPC (Marsh); estimates are Honest Cattle's, current, and descriptive, not advice.
attribution: Method from MSU Agricultural Marketing Policy Center (John Marsh); coefficients re-estimated by Honest Cattle on current USDA data. Descriptive association, not trading advice.
sources: USDA NASS Quick Stats, U.S. monthly prices received: CATTLE CALVES, CATTLE STEERS & HEIFERS GE 500 LBS, CORN GRAIN
